question: How many days did it take Meta's Threads app to reach 100 million sign-ups after it launched in July 2023?
explainer: Threads launched on 5 July 2023 and Mark Zuckerberg announced 100 million sign-ups on 10 July, the fastest start of any consumer app, helped by one-tap sign-up with an existing Instagram account.

question: How many 3.5-inch floppy disks did the retail floppy edition of Windows 95 ship on in 1995?
explainer: Microsoft used a special 1.68 MB 'DMF' disk format to squeeze Windows 95 onto 13 disks instead of the usual 1.44 MB ones; Windows NT 3.1 had needed 22 floppies two years earlier.

question: How much electricity did the world's data centres consume in 2024, according to the International Energy Agency?
source_title: IEA - Energy and AI, Executive summary
explainer: That is about 1.5% of global electricity use, roughly what France consumes in a year; the IEA expects it to more than double to about 945 TWh by 2030, driven largely by AI.

question: What was the measured HPL score (Rmax) of El Capitan, the fastest supercomputer on the November 2024 TOP500 list?
explainer: 1,742 petaflops is 1.742 quintillion floating-point calculations per second, delivered by about 11 million CPU and GPU cores at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in California.

question: How many transistors were on the Intel 4004, the first commercial microprocessor, released in 1971?
explainer: A flagship smartphone chip today has close to 20 billion transistors, roughly 8 million times more: five decades of Moore's law in a single comparison.

question: What was the launch price of the original Apple Macintosh (128K) in the United States in January 1984?
explainer: That is roughly US$7,700 in 2025 dollars; Apple had planned to sell it for $1,995 but raised the price by $500 to help pay for the launch marketing, including the famous '1984' commercial.

question: What was the price of the Motorola DynaTAC 8000X, the first commercial handheld mobile phone, when it went on sale in 1984?
explainer: About US$12,000 in today's money for a 'brick' that offered around 30 minutes of talk time and took roughly 10 hours to recharge.

question: How many vacuum tubes did ENIAC, the first general-purpose electronic computer, contain when completed in 1945?
explainer: Several tubes burned out almost every day, and the 27-tonne machine also held about 7,200 diodes, 70,000 resistors, 10,000 capacitors and around 5 million hand-soldered joints.

question: How long is the 2Africa subsea internet cable system, which encircles the African continent?
explainer: That is longer than the circumference of the Earth (40,075 km); the Meta-led cable has 46 landings in 33 countries across Africa, Europe and Asia and is the longest subsea cable system ever built.

question: How many characters are encoded in version 16.0 of the Unicode Standard, released in September 2024?
source_title: Announcing The Unicode Standard, Version 16.0 (Unicode Blog)
explainer: Unicode 16.0 added 5,185 characters, including 3,995 Egyptian hieroglyphs; emoji make up fewer than 4,000 of the total, while CJK ideographs account for nearly 100,000.

question: How many articles did the English-language Wikipedia have as of mid-2025?
explainer: The 7 millionth article, created on 24 May 2025, was about a 1958 memoir called 'Operators and Things'; English is the largest of more than 300 language editions.

question: How many copies of Wii Sports, the game bundled with the Nintendo Wii, were sold worldwide over its lifetime?
source_title: List of best-selling Wii video games - Wikipedia
explainer: Most copies came bundled with the console everywhere except Japan and South Korea, making it one of the best-selling games ever on a single platform.

question: How many daily active users did Reddit report for the fourth quarter of 2024?
source_title: Reddit Q4 and Full Year 2024 Results (Reddit Investor Relations)
explainer: Reddit calls them 'daily active uniques'; just over half are outside the United States, and the figure grew 39% in a single year.

question: How many Nintendo Switch consoles had been sold worldwide as of 31 March 2025?
source_title: Nintendo IR - Dedicated Video Game Sales Units
explainer: That puts the Switch just behind the Nintendo DS (154 million) and the PlayStation 2 (about 160 million) among the best-selling consoles of all time.

question: How many copies of Minecraft had been sold across all platforms when Mojang announced its milestone in October 2023?
explainer: That makes Minecraft the best-selling video game of all time, well ahead of Grand Theft Auto V; the previous official count was 238 million in 2021.

question: How many paid subscribers did Netflix have worldwide at the end of 2024?
source_title: Netflix Q4 2024 Shareholder Letter (Netflix Investor Relations)
explainer: Netflix added a record 19 million subscribers in the final quarter of 2024 alone, then stopped reporting quarterly subscriber counts from 2025.

question: How many smartphones were shipped worldwide in 2024, according to IDC?
explainer: That is about one new phone for every 6.5 people on Earth; Apple shipped about 232 million of them and Samsung about 223 million.

question: How many monthly active users did Facebook have as of 31 December 2023?
source_title: Meta Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2023 Results (Meta Investor Relations)
explainer: That is roughly 38% of all humans. Meta stopped reporting Facebook-only user numbers in 2024, so this is the last official figure.

question: How many people worldwide used the internet in 2024, according to the ITU's Facts and Figures 2024 report?
source_title: ITU - Measuring digital development: Facts and Figures 2024
explainer: About 68% of humanity; roughly 2.6 billion people were still offline, mostly in rural areas and low-income countries.

question: How much did Microsoft pay to acquire Activision Blizzard in the deal that closed in October 2023?
source_title: Microsoft to acquire Activision Blizzard (Microsoft News)
explainer: The largest video-game acquisition ever, about nine times Microsoft's 2021 purchase of Bethesda owner ZeniMax for $7.5 billion.

question: How many transistors are on Apple's M2 Ultra chip, released in 2023?
explainer: The M2 Ultra fuses two M2 Max dies into one; 134 billion transistors is about 58 million times the count of the 1971 Intel 4004.

question: What was Apple's total revenue in its fiscal year 2024, which ended on 28 September 2024?
source_title: Apple reports fourth quarter results, FY2024 (Apple Newsroom)
explainer: iPhone alone brought in about $201 billion; Apple's annual revenue exceeds the GDP of countries such as Finland or Portugal.

question: How many web pages had the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine archived by October 2025?
explainer: The Internet Archive marked the one-trillion-page milestone in October 2025; the Wayback Machine has been saving snapshots since 1996 and now archives hundreds of millions of URLs a day.

question: How many digits of pi were computed in the world-record calculation completed in April 2025?
source_title: Chronology of computation of pi - Wikipedia
explainer: Linus Media Group and Kioxia ran the y-cruncher program for about seven and a half months to reach 300 trillion digits; NASA uses only about 15 digits for interplanetary navigation.
